steps: Identify the shape and choose the correct formula
Substitute the measurements and work it out
Composite shapes: split into simpler shapes, then add or subtract
Units: area in cm², perimeter in cm
method_card.title: Area & Perimeter
method_card.content: Rectangle: \(A = l \times w\). Triangle: \(A = \frac{1}{2}bh\). Parallelogram: \(A = bh\). Trapezium: \(A = \frac{1}{2}(a+b)h\). Circle: \(A = \pi r^2\), \(C = 2\pi r = \pi d\).
method_card.example:
Find the area of a triangle with base 8 cm and height 5 cm.

\(A = \frac{1}{2} \times 8 \times 5 = 20\) cm².

steps: A sector is a fraction of a circle: fraction = angle ÷ 360. Sector area = fraction × π r²; arc length = fraction × 2 π r.
Working back from an area or arc: fraction = part ÷ whole, then angle = fraction × 360.
Ring (annulus): subtract the two areas, π R² − π r², never the radii.
gold.title: Gold: sectors, arcs and rings

steps.label: Check
steps.content: a 60° slice is one sixth of the circle

steps: Name the shape, then pick its formula. Rectangle: length × width. Triangle: ½ × base × height. Parallelogram: base × height. Trapezium: ½(a + b) × height.
Put the numbers in and work it out. Halve for a triangle; do not halve for a parallelogram.
Perimeter is the distance round the edge; area is the space inside. Give area in square units, like cm².

steps: Circle area is π × r²; circumference is π × d. Square the radius before multiplying by π for area.
Compound shape: work out each piece, then add or subtract. A cut-out is subtracted.
Missing radius: work backwards, r² = area ÷ π, then take the square root.

gold.hint: The arc is a fraction of the circumference; turn that fraction into an angle out of 360.

gold.hint: Subtract the two areas: pi times the outer radius squared minus pi times the inner radius squared.

Check: ring plus inner circle equals the outer circle. π × 16 + π × 9 = π × 25, to 1 d.p. =

You added the two circles. A ring subtracts the inner from the outer: π × (25 − 9) ≈ 50.3 cm².
